citations.quote: GS-US-380-1489 (Trial 1489)	MC, R, DB, AC (48 wks)	B/F/TAF (N=300)
Clinical Trials.gov identifier is NCT02607930 (EudraCT number is 2015-004024-54) for 1489

**Trial 1489** is an ongoing phase 3, randomized, double-blind study to evaluate Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Alafenamide versus Abacavir/Dolutegravir/Lamivudine in HIV-1 infected, antiretroviral treatment-naïve (TN) adults. The planned study duration is 144 weeks; however, the current NDA only provides the interim Week 48 results.

The lower bound of 2-sided 95.002% CI of the rate difference (B/F/TAF – active-control) was -4.8% in Trial 1489 and -7.9% in Trial 1490, which is greater than -12%, the pre-specified non-inferiority (NI) margin.

result.text: HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL at Week 48: 89.4% B/F/TAF vs 92.9% DTG/F/TAF; lower bound of 95.002% CI of difference -7.9% (> -12% NI margin), noninferiority demonstrated

indication.text: Complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults with no antiretroviral treatment history or to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those virologically suppressed (HIV-1 RNA less than 50 copies per mL) on a stable regimen for at least 3 months with no history of treatment failure and no known resistance substitutions

citations.quote: BIKTARVY is indicated as a complete regimen for the treatment of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in adults who have no antiretroviral treatment history or to replace the current antiretroviral regimen in those who are virologically-suppressed (HIV-1 RNA less than 50 copies per mL) on a stable antiretroviral regimen for at least 3 months with no history of treatment failure and no known substitutions associated with resistance to the individual components of BIKTARVY.

target_moa.text: Three-drug combination: bictegravir, an HIV-1 integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) that blocks the integrase enzyme responsible for insertion of the viral genome into host cell DNA, plus emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide, two nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitors

citations.quote: Bictegravir inhibits viral replication by blocking the integrase enzyme responsible for insertion of viral genome into host cell DNA.

This new drug, bictegravir, will be co-formulated in a fixed dose combination (FDC) pill with emtricitabine and tenofovir alafenamide, two approved nucleos(t)ide reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) of the HIV-1 virus
The Applicant, Gilead Sciences, submitted NDA 210251 for BIKTARVY, a fixed dose combination (FDC) tablet intended to provide a complete treatment regimen for HIV-1 infection dosed once daily.

detail.text: Post-treatment acute exacerbation of hepatitis B: severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in patients coinfected with HIV-1 and HBV who discontinued products containing emtricitabine and/or TDF, and may occur with discontinuation of BIKTARVY

citations.quote: WARNING: POST TREATMENT ACUTE EXACERBATION OF HEPATITIS B

Severe acute exacerbations of hepatitis B have been reported in patients who are coinfected with HIV-1 and HBV and have discontinued products containing emtricitabine (FTC) and/or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and may occur with discontinuation of BIKTARVY.

summary.text: BIKTARVY (NDA 210251) was reviewed as a New Molecular Entity under Priority Review, with priority review status obtained via a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher; Fast Track designation was requested but denied. No advisory committee was convened, and the drug received first-cycle approval on standard (not accelerated) approval based on four Phase 3 trials (two Phase 3 trials in treatment-naïve adults, GS-US-380-1489 and GS-US-380-1490, and two Phase 3 trials in virologically-suppressed adults, GS-US-380-1844 and GS-US-380-1878).

citations.quote: Submission Type; Type of Review	New Molecular Entity; Priority Review
This submission was accompanied with a Tropical Disease Voucher for priority review consideration.
On December 9, 2016, FDA denied this request as insufficient information was provided to support that B/F/TAF provided for an unmet medical need for the treatment of HIV-1.

The primary trials that support the safety and efficacy of the B/F/TAF (50/200/25 mg) FDC are two Phase 3 trials in HIV-1 infected, treatment-naïve adults (GS-US-380-1489 and GS-US-380-1490) and two Phase 3 trials in HIV-1 infected, virologically suppressed adults (GS-US-380-1844 and GS-US-380-1878).
